content: 1. Document the patient's past medical history and family history, specifically in the context of diabetes, as per the American Diabetes Association (ADA) guidelines. 2. Record any personal history of diabetes-related complications and commonly associated comorbidities. 3. Identify and document comorbid conditions such as obesity, sleep apnea, and liver disease. 4. 5. Screen for both cardiovascular and microvascular complications that may arise as a result of diabetes. 6. Assess the patient’s awareness of hypoglycemia, as well as the frequency, causes, and timing of hypoglycemic episodes. 7. Evaluate for hematologic conditions, including hemoglobinopathies or anemia, which may impact overall health. 8. Record the dates and findings of the patient’s most recent eye and dental examinations. 9. 10. Assess the patient’s use of any assistive devices, such as mobility aids, and evaluate their functional status or disability.
